newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican condemns second Australian suicide.
newsitem.headline: Vatican condemns second Australian suicide.

text.p: The Vatican condemned the second death under Australia's world-first euthanasia law as a revolt against God on Tuesday and urged opponents to campaign harder against the threatened "contagion" of assisted suicide.

"To decide one's own death and obtain it, even with recourse to the law and medical assistance, is an act of revolt against God, author of life, and a crime against life," moral theologian Gino Concetti wrote in the newspaper L'Osservatore Romano.

He was responding to an announcement by euthanasia campaigners on Monday that 52-year-old Janet Mills had become the second person to die under the Northern Territory's euthanasia law, which came into force last July.
Mills, who had been suffering from a rare form of skin cancer, used a device driven by a laptop computer to deliver a fatal dose of drugs last Thursday, the campaigners said.

In September, 66-year-old cancer patient Bob Dent became the first person to use the Territory's Rights of the Terminally Ill Act to die. An alliance of church and civic leaders is leading a legal and parliamentary battle to quash the law.
Concetti, who is close to Pope John Paul, said no law could legitimise assisted suicide "without overturning the principles of civilisation".
"The risk of contagion is anything but remote," he wrote in the Vatican's semi-official daily newspaper.
"That is what increases the responsibility of those who believe in the values of life and regard the culture of death as an unacceptable and devastating degradation," Concetti wrote.
